title: WAF-blocked request with matched rule, anomaly score, and bot verdict
event_type: WAF/CDN edge console — blocked-request detail view (e.g., ModSecurity CRS-style engine)

callouts.explanation: A plain origin access log has no concept of a 'matched rule' — this field only exists because a WAF layer sits in front of the origin and makes an allow/block decision based on signature matching.

The anomaly/risk score is a WAF-specific computed value (common in CRS-style engines) that aggregates multiple weak signals into a single decision threshold — a plain access log has no equivalent field.

Bot-classification verdicts require behavioral/fingerprinting analysis a plain web server never performs, illustrating why a WAF-fronted log is a structurally different data source, not the same log with extra columns.

note: Illustrative/conceptual mockup of a WAF/CDN console blocked-request view; not a captured screenshot of any real vendor product.
